title: Vanishing conormal for flat morphism with open diagonal
statement: Let f:X → S be a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism] whose diagonal is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For any universal first order thickening i:X → X′, s:X′ → S of f [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], its conormal sheaf i*(ker i) [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified, def-pc-module-pullback] is zero. Finite type is not needed: the open diagonal already implies formal unramifiedness [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism].

proof.text: The open diagonal implies FormallyUnramified f by the Mathlib open-diagonal instance (FormallyUnramified.lean:79); no finite type is used. *The diagonal and the two projections.* Let $p,q:X\times_SX\to X$ be the first and the second projection of the fibre product of $f$ with itself [def-pc-fibre-product], and $\Delta=(\mathrm{id}_X,\mathrm{id}_X):X\to X\times_SX$ the diagonal, so $p\circ\Delta=q\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$. By hypothesis, $\Delta$ is an open immersion  (Stacks quotes Morphisms, Lemma 02GE here, which with the definition of the DAG is part of the definition) [def-weil-open-immersion]; let $D=\Delta(X)\subset X\times_SX$ be the open subscheme it defines and $\delta:X\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ the induced isomorphism, so $\Delta=j\circ\delta$ with $j:D\to X\times_SX$ the inclusion. The morphism $q$ is the base change of $f$ along $f$ (the projection of $X\times_SX$ to the second factor), so $q$ is formally unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-base-change] applied to the formally unramified $f$ of step 1. The morphism $p$ is the base change of the flat morphism $f$ along $f$ (projection to the first factor), so $p$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *$p^*\mathcal C_{X/S}\cong\mathcal C_q$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-flat-base-change] to the fibre product square with $Y=S$, $W=X$ (the first factor) with the formally unramified morphism $h'=f:W\to S$, and the flat morphism $g=f:X\to S$ (the second factor): then $Z=X\times_SX$, the projection $Z\to X$ to the second factor is $h=q$, and the projection to $W$ is $p$. The lemma gives that $q$ is formally unramified (also seen in step 2) and that the canonical map $p^*\mathcal C_{X/S}\to\mathcal C_q$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X\times_SX}$-modules, where $\mathcal C_q=\mathcal C_{X\times_SX/X}$ is the conormal sheaf of the formally unramified morphism $q$ [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified], [def-pc-module-pullback]. (Stacks cites Lemma 04F9 together with the flatness of $p$, which is the flatness of $g$ in the lemma.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *$\mathcal C_q|_D=0$.* The open subscheme $D=\Delta(X)$ maps isomorphically to $X$ under $q$: $q|_D\circ\delta=q\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\delta$ is an isomorphism, so $e:=q|_D:D\to X$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\delta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-universal-thickening-open-restriction] applied to $q$ with $V=D$ and $U=X$, $e$ is formally unramified and $\mathcal C_q|_D\cong\mathcal C_{D/X}$. Now $D\subset D$ (identity closed immersion, ideal sheaf $0$) with structure morphism $e$ is a universal first order thickening of $D$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]: given a first order thickening $T\subset T'$ over $X$ with $i_T:T\to T'$, $b:T'\to X$, and $a:T\to D$ with $e\circ a=b\circ i_T$, the morphism $a'=e^{-1}\circ b$ satisfies $e\circ a'=b$ and $a'\circ i_T=e^{-1}\circ e\circ a=a$, and it is the only one since $e\circ a'=b$ forces $a'=e^{-1}\circ b$. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening-exists] every universal first order thickening of $D$ over $X$ is isomorphic to this one compatibly with $D$, so the ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] of $D$ in it is $0$ and $\mathcal C_{D/X}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified]. Hence $\mathcal C_q|_D=0$ ('$\mathcal C_q|_{\Delta(X)}=\mathcal C_{X/X}=0$' in Stacks, by Lemma 04FA).

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale)

proof.text: *$\mathcal C_{X/S}=0$.* Pullback of modules satisfies $\mathrm{id}^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $(v\circ u)^*\cong u^*v^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Since $p\circ\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\Delta=j\circ\delta$, steps 3 and 4 give $\mathcal C_{X/S}\cong\Delta^*p^*\mathcal C_{X/S}\cong\Delta^*\mathcal C_q\cong\delta^*j^*\mathcal C_q\cong\delta^*(\mathcal C_q|_D)=\delta^*0=0$, where $j^*\mathcal C_q\cong\mathcal C_q|_D$ because $j$ is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]. ('In other words, the pullback of $\mathcal C_{X/S}$ to $X$ via the identity morphism is zero, i.e., $\mathcal C_{X/S}=0$.')

theorem flat_openDiagonal_conormal_isZero {X S X' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal f)]
    (i : X ⟶ X') (s : X' ⟶ S) (H : IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening f i s) :
    IsZero (formallyUnramifiedConormal f i s H)
